title: enzyme-catalyzed synthesis of unsaturated aliphatic polyesters based on green monomers from renewable resources
display_name: Enzyme-Catalyzed Synthesis of Unsaturated Aliphatic Polyesters Based on Green Monomers from Renewable Resources
abstract: bio-based commercially available succinate, itaconate and 1,4-butanediol are enzymatically co-polymerized in solution via a two-stage method, using candida antarctica lipase b (calb, in immobilized form as novozyme 435) as the biocatalyst. the chemical structures of the obtained products, poly(butylene succinate) (pbs) and poly(butylene succinate-co-itaconate) (pbsi), are confirmed by 1h- and 13c-nmr. the effects of the reaction conditions on the calb-catalyzed synthesis of pbsi are fully investigated, and the optimal polymerization conditions are obtained. with the established method, pbsi with tunable compositions and satisfying reaction yields is produced. the 1h-nmr results confirm that carbon-carbon double bonds are well preserved in pbsi. the differential scanning calorimetry (dsc) and thermal gravimetric analysis (tga) results indicate that the amount of itaconate in the co-polyesters has no obvious effects on the glass-transition temperature and the thermal stability of pbs and pbsi, but has significant effects on the melting temperature.

title: chitosan biopolymer promotes yield and stimulates accumulation of antioxidants in strawberry fruit
display_name: Chitosan biopolymer promotes yield and stimulates accumulation of antioxidants in strawberry fruit
abstract: strawberry is a well-known source of natural antioxidants with excellent free radical scavenging capacity. this study determined the effects of chitosan application in field condition on plant growth, fruit yield and antioxidant activities in strawberry fruit. foliar applications of chitosan on strawberry significantly increased plant growth and fruit yield (up to 42% higher) compared to untreated control. increased fruit yield was attributed to higher plant growth, individual fruit weight and total fruit weight/plant due to the chitosan application. surprisingly, the fruit from plants sprayed with chitosan also had significantly higher contents (up to 2.6-fold) of carotenoids, anthocyanins, flavonoids and phenolics compared to untreated control. total antioxidant activities in fruit of chitosan treated plants were also significantly higher (ca. 2-fold) (p< 0.05) than untreated control. to the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of chitosan applied on field plants providing significant improvement of both yield and health benefiting biochemical contents in strawberry fruit. further study on the elucidation of mechanisms involved with enhancement of growth, yield and biochemical contents by chitosan is needed to promote sustainable production of strawberry.

title: transparent exopolymer particles and dissolved organic carbon production by emiliania huxleyi exposed to different co2 concentrations: a mesocosm experiment
display_name: Transparent exopolymer particles and dissolved organic carbon production by Emiliania huxleyi exposed to different CO2 concentrations: a mesocosm experiment

authorships.name: Anja Engel
institutions: Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung

authorships.name: Stéphan Jacquet
institutions: Institut National de la Recherche Agronomique

authorships.name: Ulf Riebesell
institutions: Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung

authorships.name: A Terbrüggen
institutions: Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung

authorships.name: Ingrid Zondervan
institutions: Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung

abstract: the role of transparent exopolymer particles (tep) and dissolved organic carbon (doc) for organic carbon partitioning under different co2 conditions was examined during a mesocosm experiment with the coccolithophorid emiliania huxleyi. we designed 9 outdoor enclosures (similar to11 m(3)) to simulate co2 concentrations of estimated 'year 2100' (similar to710 ppm co2), 'present' (similar to410 ppm co2) and 'glacial' (similar to190 ppm co2) environments, and fertilized these with nitrate and phosphate to favor bloom development. our results showed fundamentally different tep and doc dynamics during the bloom. in all mesocosms, tep concentration increased after nutrient exhaustion and accumulated steadily until the end of the study. tep concentration was closely related to the abundance of e. huxleyi and accounted for an increase in poc concentration of 35 +/- 2 % after the onset of nutrient limitation. the production of tep normalized to the cell abundance of e. huxleyi was highest in the year 2100 treatment. in contrast, doc concentration exhibited considerable short-term fluctuations throughout the study. in all mesocosms, doc was neither related to the abundance of e. huxleyi nor to tep concentration. a statistically significant effect of the co2 treatment on doc concentration was not determined. however, during the course of the bloom, doc concentration increased in 2 of the 3 year 2100 mesocosms and in 1 of the present mesocosms, but in none of the glacial mesocosms. it is suggested that the observed differences between tep and doc were determined by their different bioavailability and that a rapid response of the microbial food web may have obscured co2 effects on doc production by autotrophic cells.

title: global seaweed farming and processing in the past 20 years
display_name: Global seaweed farming and processing in the past 20 years
abstract: abstract seaweed has emerged as one of the most promising resources due to its remarkable adaptability, short development period, and resource sustainability. it is an effective breakthrough to alleviate future resource crises. algal resources have reached a high stage of growth in the past years due to the increased output and demand for seaweed worldwide. several aspects global seaweed farming production and processing over the last 20 years are reviewed, such as the latest situation and approaches of seaweed farming. research progress and production trend of various seaweed application are discussed. besides, the challenges faced by seaweed farming and processing are also analyzed, and the related countermeasures are proposed, which can provide advice for seaweed farming and processing. the primary products, extraction and application, or waste utilization of seaweed would bring greater benefits with the continuous development and improvement of applications in various fields. graphical abstract

title: the athlete s diet: nutritional goals and dietary strategies
display_name: The athlete’s diet: nutritional goals and dietary strategies
abstract: when talented, motivated and highly trained athletes meet for competition the margin between victory and defeat is usually small. when everything else is equal, nutrition can make the difference between winning and losing. although the primary concern of many athletes is to supplement the diet with protein, vitamins and minerals, and a range of more exotic compounds, key dietary issues are often neglected. athletes must establish their nutritional goals, and must also be able to translate them into dietary strategies that will meet these goals. athletes are often concerned with dietary manipulations in the period around competition, but the main role of nutrition may be to support consistent intensive training which will lead to improved performance. meeting energy demand and maintaining body mass and body fat at appropriate levels are key goals. an adequate intake of carbohydrate is crucial for maintaining muscle glycogen stores during hard training, but the types of food and the timing of intake are also important. protein ingestion may stimulate muscle protein synthesis in the post-exercise period, promoting the process of adaptation in the muscles. restoration of fluid and electrolyte balance after exercise is essential. if energy intake is high and a varied diet is consumed, supplementation of the diet with vitamins and minerals is not warranted, unless a specific deficiency is identified. specific strategies before competition may be necessary, but this requirement depends on the demands of the sport. generally, it is important to ensure high pre-competition glycogen stores and to maintain fluid balance. there is limited evidence to support the use of dietary supplements, but some, including perhaps creatine and caffeine, may be beneficial.

title: co-ordinated expression of amino acid metabolism in response to n and s deficiency during wheat grain filling
display_name: Co-ordinated expression of amino acid metabolism in response to N and S deficiency during wheat grain filling
abstract: increasing demands for productivity together with environmental concerns about fertilizer use dictate that the future sustainability of agricultural systems will depend on improving fertilizer use efficiency. characterization of the biological processes responsible for efficient fertilizer use will provide tools for crop improvement under reduced inputs. transcriptomic and metabolomic approaches were used to study the impact of nitrogen (n) and sulphur (s) deficiency on n and s remobilization from senescing canopy tissues during grain filling in winter wheat (triticum aestivum). canopy tissue n was remobilized effectively to the grain after anthesis. s was less readily remobilized. nuclear magnetic resonance (nmr) metabolite profiling revealed significant effects of suboptimal n or s supply in leaves but not in developing grain. analysis of amino acid pools in the grain and leaves revealed a strategy whereby amino acid biosynthesis switches to the production of glutamine during grain filling. glutamine accumulated in the first 7 d of grain development, prior to conversion to other amino acids and protein in the subsequent 21 d. transcriptome analysis indicated that a down-regulation of the terminal steps in many amino acid biosynthetic pathways occurs to control pools of amino acids during leaf senescence. grain n and s contents increased in parallel after anthesis and were not significantly affected by s deficiency, despite a suboptimal n:s ratio at final harvest. n deficiency resulted in much slower accumulation of grain n and s and lower final concentrations, indicating that vegetative tissue n has a greater control of the timing and extent of nutrient remobilization than s.

title: a brief biography of bruce merrifield: his life and legacy
display_name: A brief biography of Bruce Merrifield: His life and legacy
abstract: in this special memorial issue of biopolymers: peptide science we commemorate the scientific life and achievements of bruce merrifield. his impact on the direction of scientific research being undertaken today in a multitude of research laboratories and pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies throughout the world is of such a profound nature that it is not possible to encompass his contributions in a single edition. almost as important is the impact that bruce merrifield has had on the careers of numerous distinguished scientists who have been influenced by his work ethic, his encouragement, and his humility, all of which provide a legacy for the future of our field. many of those colleagues who were privileged to have spent time working and collaborating with bruce have authored manuscripts that are included in this special issue. i personally had the good fortune of spending 1 year in the merrifield laboratory. it was unquestionably the most important year of my scientific career, a sentiment that is undoubtedly shared by my colleagues who spent time in the merrifield laboratory. on november 13, 2006, merrifield alumni had the opportunity to celebrate bruce's scientific life and achievements at a special symposium, a tribute to bruce merrifield, held at the rockefeller university. the following brief biography is excerpted from that presentation (see ref.1 for a complete autobiography). bruce merrifield was born in fort worth, texas, on july 15, 1921. his father, george evan merrifield, served in france during world war i, then enrolled in business college in fort worth to prepare for a career in sales. his mother, mittie lorene lucas, was graduated from texas state college for women as an art major. in the spring of 1923, the family set out for california in an air-cooled franklin automobile on unpaved roads in search of employment opportunities. they settled down and bought a home in santa barbara, california, where his father was employed as a furniture salesman and interior decorator. growing up during the great depression had a profound influence on young bruce merrifield. these were difficult times, and beginning in 1928 the family had to relocate in the pursuit of employment. by the time he enrolled in montebello high school in southern california, the family had moved 25 times and bruce had attended 11 different schools. at montebello high school, he was exposed to his first chemistry class and was immediately intrigued. he also joined the astronomy club and finished second in the annual science competition. following high school graduation, bruce enrolled in pasadena junior college. upon completion of the 2-year program there, he transferred to ucla, a new branch of the california state university system. ucla had an excellent chemistry faculty including william young, who was department chairman, and max dunn, professor of biochemistry. following his graduation in 1943 with a bachelor's degree, bruce took a job as a laboratory technician at the philip park research foundation in san pedro, california. his responsibilities included maintaining rat and chicken colonies: feeding, weighing, and cleaning their cages. his project involved studies on the importance of essential amino acids on the growth of the laboratory animals. his studies showed that there was no net growth in the absence of even one essential amino acid from their diet. at the end of the year, bruce reflected on his future and realized that if he were to design his own experiments he must return to graduate school. bruce received a teaching assistantship on his return to graduate school to assist max dunn in the biochemistry course at ucla. this was an important appointment since elizabeth (libby) furlong, a very pretty girl with long red hair, was enrolled in the class.1 libby has stated that she was immediately infatuated by the teaching assistant who was sitting in the back of the room. they enjoyed tennis, ice-skating, hiking, and camping in the nearby mountains, and dancing together to the big band music of the 1940s. libby successfully completed her master's degree in zoology and began working on her doctorate. with his first paycheck from a temporary job at ucla, bruce bought a ring and proposed (figure 1). over the years, bruce and libby had six children. camping trips became one of the main family activities. the merrifield's enjoyed camping in the adirondacks, white mountains, mount kahtadin, grand canyon, mesa verde, yellowstone, grand tetons, and many other national parks including a memorable trip on alaska's alcan highway to mount mckinley. many of these trips were shared with their children and sixteen grandchildren. bruce and libby celebrating their engagement at coconut grove night club in los angeles, ca (december, 1948). photo courtesy of elizabeth merrifield. bruce's ph.d. thesis work under the supervision of max dunn involved the development of new microbiological methods to analyze for the pyrimidine bases that are present in all nucleotides. his studies included the use of various strains of bacteria for quantitative determination of the pyrimidines. this was an important topic at the time. eventually, erwin chargaff developed methods to analyze for both purine and pyrimidine bases. this innovation led to the chargaff rules that provided an important groundwork for the eventual elucidation of dna structure by watson and crick. just prior to bruce's completion of the ph.d. program, dr. d. w. woolley of the rockefeller institute for medical research was looking for a research assistant. upon the recommendation of max dunn, bruce was offered a one-year postdoctoral research assistantship commencing july 1, 1949. dr. woolley was a pioneer in vitamin research, an authority on antimetabolites, and an expert on the pharmacology of serotonin. on june 19, 1949, bruce was graduated from ucla with his ph.d., and on the next day, june 20, bruce and libby were married. on the following day, june 21, they left for new york city in their 1935 ford on a camping honeymoon starting at yosemite national park with a final stop at a diner in new jersey, where they both came down with food poisoning. in 1949, the rockefeller institute for medical research was steeped in tradition. there was a formal dining room in founder's hall that provided an ideal setting to meet colleagues from different areas of research and bruce met many famous people there, including ren dubos, lyman craig, william stein, stanford moore, and many others. bruce's entire academic career unfolded on the rockefeller campus and was totally dedicated to the institution. dr. woolley, who bruce considered to be the most brilliant man he has known, was a major influence on his career. bruce's one-year postdoctoral research assistantship was extended and he was appointed assistant professor, and then promoted to associate professor in 1958, and full professor in 1966. bruce's major project involved studies on a new bacterial growth factor, streptogenin, which was previously discovered by dr. woolley. fractionation of the factor resulted in the isolation of two highly active insulin fragments, a heptapeptide and a homologous pentapeptide. it was necessary to confirm the structure of these peptides by chemical synthesis. his first introduction to peptide synthesis involved a tedious fragment synthesis of the pentapeptide, which required 11 months for its completion and was obtained with an overall yield of only 7%. the need for a better, faster, more efficient synthesis of peptides became apparent to bruce. in 1959, he conceived the idea of carrying out peptide synthesis on a solid support. his fundamental idea was to covalently link the terminal amino acid at the cooh-terminus to the solid support. subsequent attachment of additional n-protected amino acids could be carried out using suitable activation procedures in a stepwise fashion until the desired peptide sequence was assembled. the procedure would avoid the need to purify intermediates, and that excess reagents and byproducts could be removed by thorough washing of the solid support with appropriate solvents. it is noteworthy that he documented the entire concept in his laboratory notebook on may 26, 1959 (figure 2). bruce initially thought the procedure, which he named solid phase peptide synthesis, could be developed in about 3 months, but there were unforeseen challenges at every stage. a compatible solid support, efficient coupling methods, appropriate protecting groups, suitable solvents, and conditions for the removal of the final peptide from the solid support all had to be developed almost simultaneously. laboratory notebook entry by bruce detailing his plans for solid-phase peptide synthesis (may 26, 1959). in 1963, bruce published his seminal paper2 that described the synthesis of the first tetrapeptide by the solid-phase procedure and is among the most cited papers in the literature. the rockefeller university has been recognized by the acs division of the history of chemistry with a citation for chemical breakthroughs for this publication. although the new methodology was enthusiastically received by many prominent scientists, several established peptide chemists were skeptical and even critical of the solid-phase concept. at an early stage in its development, bruce recognized the feasibility of automating solid-phase peptide synthesis and, together with john stewart at the rockefeller university, constructed the first automated synthesizer.3 this provided an important groundwork for the development of commercial instruments, including batch and continuous flow synthesizers. bruce spent much of his career developing and improving the new methodology. bruce, together with bernd gutte, tested the limits of the methodology with the total synthesis of the entire 124-residue enzyme, bovine pancreatic ribonuclease a. the synthesis of this enzyme, which possessed nearly full biological potency,4 was a milestone achievement. subsequent work from the merrifield laboratory included optimization of solid-phase peptide synthesis and applying the methodology to solving biological problems related to peptides and proteins. at an early stage, bruce recognized the importance of using solid-phase chemistry to direct organic syntheses in general. solid-phase techniques are currently being used for the preparation of combinatorial libraries that are used for drug discovery and for the preparation of biomacromolecules, including carbohydrates and nucleic acids. on october 17, 1984, bruce and libby missed the telephone call from stockholm informing him of his selection for the 1984 nobel prize in chemistry. they were delayed in traffic on their daily commute to the laboratory and only learned about it as they stepped off the elevator on the fourth floor of flexner hall at the rockefeller university. in retrospect, hearing the good news from his associates and colleagues in the laboratory was the most appropriate setting for bruce, since working in the laboratory was of paramount importance to him. recognition with the nobel prize represented the ultimate acceptance of his work by his peers and his inclusion with other distinguished chemists whom he held in high esteem. bruce was presented with the nobel medal on december 10, 1984, by king carl xvi gustaf at the royal concert hall in stockholm (figure 3). bruce confided to me that he was fascinated by queen silvia, whom he escorted to the banquet hall. presentation of nobel prize to bruce merrifield by king karl gustaf xvi (december 10, 1984). photo courtesy of jan collsi /scanpix/retna. bruce merrifield revolutionized chemistry and thereby has had a major impact on the direction of scientific research in biochemistry, molecular biology, pharmacology, and medicine. he has trained numerous graduate and postdoctoral students and influenced a generation of peptide scientists who have become leaders in academia and industry. his visit in 1968 to my laboratory at hoffmann-la roche (figure 4) was an inspiration to me and my colleagues and left a lasting impression. in her editorial in a recent edition of biopolymers/peptide science,5 lila gierasch referred to bruce as the gentle giant of peptide science. this is a most accurate description of this hard working, humble scientist who has influenced the field of peptide science and raised it to its highest level. bruce's career stands as a model that demonstrates the importance of believing in your idea, overcoming criticisms by respected colleagues, improving and optimizing the idea, and demonstrating its importance and application to the solution of relevant problems in your area of research. a giant of the magnitude of bruce merrifield comes only once in a generation. chemists, now and in the future, will owe a debt of gratitude to the legacy of bruce merrifield. bruce merrifield with art felix inspecting an early batch solid-phase synthesis apparatus at hoffmann-la roche (1968). photo courtesy of dr. arthur felix.

title: cellulase linkers are optimized based on domain type and function: insights from sequence analysis, biophysical measurements, and molecular simulation
display_name: Cellulase Linkers Are Optimized Based on Domain Type and Function: Insights from Sequence Analysis, Biophysical Measurements, and Molecular Simulation
abstract: cellulase enzymes deconstruct cellulose to glucose, and are often comprised of glycosylated linkers connecting glycoside hydrolases (ghs) to carbohydrate-binding modules (cbms). although linker modifications can alter cellulase activity, the functional role of linkers beyond domain connectivity remains unknown. here we investigate cellulase linkers connecting gh family 6 or 7 catalytic domains to family 1 or 2 cbms, from both bacterial and eukaryotic cellulases to identify conserved characteristics potentially related to function. sequence analysis suggests that the linker lengths between structured domains are optimized based on the gh domain and cbm type, such that linker length may be important for activity. longer linkers are observed in eukaryotic gh family 6 cellulases compared to gh family 7 cellulases. bacterial gh family 6 cellulases are found with structured domains in either n to c terminal order, and similar linker lengths suggest there is no effect of domain order on length. o-glycosylation is uniformly distributed across linkers, suggesting that glycans are required along entire linker lengths for proteolysis protection and, as suggested by simulation, for extension. sequence comparisons show that proline content for bacterial linkers is more than double that observed in eukaryotic linkers, but with fewer putative o-glycan sites, suggesting alternative methods for extension. conversely, near linker termini where linkers connect to structured domains, o-glycosylation sites are observed less frequently, whereas glycines are more prevalent, suggesting the need for flexibility to achieve proper domain orientations. putative n-glycosylation sites are quite rare in cellulase linkers, while an n-p motif, which strongly disfavors the attachment of n-glycans, is commonly observed. these results suggest that linkers exhibit features that are likely tailored for optimal function, despite possessing low sequence identity. this study suggests that cellulase linkers may exhibit function in enzyme action, and highlights the need for additional studies to elucidate cellulase linker functions.

title: early development of biochemistry and molecular biology in israel
display_name: Early development of biochemistry and molecular biology in Israel
abstract: professor chaim weizmann (1874 1952), the first president of the state of israel and an organic chemist by profession, championed the idea of creating modern scientific centers that could help build a country lacking natural resources (1). weizmann, in his role then as the president of the world zionist organization, was one of the central figures that supported the founding of the hebrew university of jerusalem. in 1924, the university established the institute for chemical research on mount scopus, which included a department for biological and colloid chemistry (1-5). after discussions with albert einstein, carl neuberg, richard willstt ter, and other prominent scientists, weizmann also led to the establishment of the daniel sieff research center in rehovot, modeled after the kaiser-wilhelm-gesellschaft institutes established in germany during the earliest years of the 20th century. ten years later, in the spring of 1934, the very first building of what would later develop into the weizmann institute campus was inaugurated by the opening of the daniel sieff research institute. it employed 10 tenured scientists who were involved with chemical, biochemical, and pharmaceutical studies (6). the sieff institute located at the village of rehovot, surrounded by orange groves, about 21 km south east of tel-aviv, was within walking distance from the agricultural experimental station of the jewish agency. this station came into existence in 1921, and in 1926 had a staff of 38 scientists and agronomists (7). it was hoped that the close proximity of the two institutions would lead to collaboration in their research efforts. during world war ii, the scientists of the sieff institute were heavily involved in the war efforts, especially in the production of the antimalarial drug atabrine and other essential pharmaceuticals. biochemistry teaching and research started in the early part of the 20th century in british ruled palestine by a small number of idealistically motivated scientists emigrating from europe, before the nazi rise to power, and founded the nucleus of the hebrew university of jerusalem. already in 1923, professor andor fodor (1884 1964) came from the university of halle, germany, and joined the budding hebrew university of jerusalem. he established the institute for chemical research, served as both as its director and head of what later became the department for biological and colloid chemistry. fodor was the first research professor appointed at the hebrew university. the modest institute he directed consisted of a small staff of two tenured assistants, max frankel and adolf reifenberg, and a small number of research associates as well as volunteer workers. frankel (1900 1972) obtained his ph.d. degree from the university of vienna and worked at this university's institute of chemical technology before immigrating to palestine. at the hebrew university, he was appointed to direct the laboratory of theoretical and macromolecular chemistry. reifenberg, who was awarded a ph.d. by the university of giessen, germany, was in charge of the laboratory of applied biological and colloid chemistry that focused its studies on agricultural chemistry. upon the arrival at the hebrew university, fodor initiated lecture courses in biochemistry for the third year students and continued his research that he had started in halle, of peptide chemistry and synthesis. his theories of protein structure as well as the possible involvement of a colloid carrier in enzyme activity were influenced by the ideas proposed by richard willstt ter that, unfortunately, were not well received (confer 3). it took a considerable amount of time, dedication, and efforts to create comprehensive biochemistry lectures and laboratory courses. thus, nucleic acid metabolism and enzymology were introduced to the students considerably later at the end of the 1950s (4, 5). frankel joined fodor as junior assistant in the fall of 1925 and was promoted to the rank of professor in 1953. he had wide interests in many areas of classical and theoretical organic chemistry. in particular, he concentrated on the study of high molecular weight synthetic polymers, their polymerization mechanisms, and properties as well as their possible practical applications in the plastic industry. in parallel, he dedicated himself to the teaching of organic chemistry. several years after fodor's arrival, ernst wertheimer (1893 1978), also from the university of halle, was appointed professor of pathological physiology at the hebrew university and as director of the laboratory of chemistry of the hadassa hospital in jerusalem. he taught physiological chemistry at the hebrew university-hadassa medical school in jerusalem, which was the only one in the country at that time (nowadays, there are four). together with his assistant, benjamin shapiro (1913 1993), they conducted their research on the metabolism and enzymology of adipose tissue as well as the hormonal regulation of lipids in man and animals (8). yeshayahu leibovitz (1903 1995) was another german educated scientist who joined the hebrew university in 1934. he received his ph.d. degree at the university of berlin and was well known for his studies on carbohydrate metabolism, first at the university of berlin and later, in the famous laboratory of carl neuberg at the kaiser wilhelm institute for biochemistry in dahlem. at the hebrew university, leibovitz introduced a detailed lecture course on carbohydrate chemistry as well as general biochemistry and continued his productive research particularly on the specificity of hydrolytic enzymes that degrade di- and polysaccharides (see, e.g., (9). for many years, leibovitz was also involved in lecturing and writing on a range of philosophical and political issues that always attracted large audiences. ernst david bergmann (1903 1976) was a brilliant organic chemist characterized by great scientific productivity. he was a former student of wilhelm schlenk, at the university of berlin, with whom he also coauthored an important textbook of organic chemistry. bergmann had an exceptionally energetic and creative personality with an encyclopedic knowledge of chemistry and broad interest in science. in 1933, he was approached by chaim weizmann to help plan and direct the sieff institute and later also served as the first scientific director of the weizmann institute (10). bergmann left an exceptional impact on the scientific development of israel in a wide range of fields and served as professor of organic chemistry at the hebrew university of jerusalem till his untimely death. in the early years of the hebrew university existence, the number of students was rather small. thus, in 1944, the chemistry class was limited to 23 students. moreover, employment opportunities in british mandatory palestine were uncertain. still, a high proportion of the students matured to become internationally recognized for their own research. frankel's most famous israeli educated students were the katzir brothers, aharon katzir-katchalsky (1913 1972), and ephraim katchalski-katzir (b. 1916). both brothers became known for their original research and wide interest in biological problems as well as in science policy. later, in 1948, both brothers joined the weizmann institute. aharon katzir distinguished himself as a chemist, mainly interested in macromolecules and was one of the institute's most eminent scientists, where he founded the department of polymer chemistry. in his studies, he applied modern developments of nonequilibrium thermodynamics to consideration of biological problems (11). he was also instrumental in founding the israel academy of sciences and humanities. from 1964 to 1969, he served as president of the international union of pure and applied biophysics (iupab). his brilliant and dynamic career ended tragically when japanese red army terrorists assassinated him in 1972 at the ben-gurion airport near tel aviv. ephraim katzir occupies a leading position among israeli scientists for his outstanding work on the synthesis and characterization of polyamino acids, which he used as models for the structure and function of proteins (12). in 1948, he joined the weizmann institute of science and founded its department of biophysics that became internationally acclaimed for its excellent achievements and attracted many foreign scholars. he is also known for his contributions to the development of immobilized enzymes that found application for many industrial purposes (13). ephraim katzir received a great number of prestigious awards and, in 1973, was elected to be the fourth president of the state of israel. upon completion of his 5-year term, he returned to research, which he is continuing until this very day (12, 13). shlomo hestrin (1914 1962) occupies a unique position among the israeli educated scientists for introducing modern enzyme research in israel. he entered the hebrew university in 1933 and received his m.sc. and ph.d. degrees under the guidance of leibovitz, investigating the fermentation of di- and polysaccharides. in 1949, hestrin spent some time in the laboratory of nobel laureates gerty theresa cori and carl ferdinand cori at the george washington university school of medicine, st. louis, mo, as well as in the laboratory of david nachmansohn at columbia university, new york. he developed a hydroxamate method for the determination of active esters that is widely in use until today. later on, with his students, he investigated the mechanism of synthesis of cellulose by acetobacter xylinum. all these earned him international standing (14). in 1959, hestrin succeeded fodor as head of the department of biological chemistry at the hebrew university of jerusalem. nucleic acid research at the weizmann institute was intensified when, in 1957, a new section of biochemistry was founded. it consisted originally of four independent groups, with theodore winnick (formerly, of iowa state college), as the head. his group studied protein and peptide biosynthesis. another group, led by david elson (a former student of erwin chargaff), dealt with the structure and function of the ribosome. mordehay avron whose interests centered on bioenergetics, primarily the mechanism of photosynthesis led another group (4). a group, led by uriel littauer (a former post doctoral fellow in arthur kornberg's lab) investigated the enzymatic synthesis of rna, the physicochemical characterization of rrna and trna, and their relation to protein synthesis (4). this brief review needs to end with a brief note on recent years' development of israel's life science-based industry. israel has some of the world's finest scientific infra structures benefiting from a firm correlation between the academia, medical institutions, and industry. in fact, israel is ranked second and third in terms of number of publications in leading life science magazines per 100,000 inhabitants and senior faculty members per million inhabitants, respectively. the relatively fast growth of academic and clinical research in israel during the recent decades also prompted a rather impressive development of israeli industry centered on a broad band of life science-related aspects. it ranges from the development of sophisticated medical devices to agricultural, pharmaceutical, and medical service companies. fundamental research at universities and private research institutions yielded a wealth of intellectual property in biochemistry, molecular biology, or immunology. this, in turn, led to the development of a myriad of hundreds of companies that are active in efforts of converting this know-how into commercial products. this is naturally leading to the development of providers of services to such innovative industry starting from venture capitalists, lawyers, accountants, and incubators. to date, more than 900 companies, ranging in size, have been established, addressing aspects of pharmaceuticals, biotechnology and agricultural biotechnology, medical information technology, and medical or diagnostic devices. just in the realm of biotechnology, these companies are involved in research and development of vaccines, novel antibodies, drug-discovery, gene therapy, bioinformatics as well as genomics, proteomics, and glycomics.

title: contributions of organic and inorganic matter to sediment volume and accretion in tidal wetlands at steady state
display_name: Contributions of organic and inorganic matter to sediment volume and accretion in tidal wetlands at steady state
abstract: abstract a mixing model derived from first principles describes the bulk density ( bd ) of intertidal wetland sediments as a function of loss on ignition ( loi ). the model assumes that the bulk volume of sediment equates to the sum of self packing volumes of organic and mineral components or bd = 1/[ loi / k 1 + (1 loi )/ k 2 ], where k 1 and k 2 are the self packing densities of the pure organic and inorganic components, respectively. the model explained 78% of the variability in total bd when fitted to 5075 measurements drawn from 33 wetlands distributed around the conterminous united states. the values of k 1 and k 2 were estimated to be 0.085 0.0007 g cm 3 and 1.99 0.028 g cm 3 , respectively. based on the fitted organic density ( k 1 ) and constrained by primary production, the model suggests that the maximum steady state accretion arising from the sequestration of refractory organic matter is 0.3 cm yr 1 . thus, tidal peatlands are unlikely to indefinitely survive a higher rate of sea level rise in the absence of a significant source of mineral sediment. application of k 2 to a mineral sediment load typical of east and eastern gulf coast estuaries gives a vertical accretion rate from inorganic sediment of 0.2 cm yr 1 . total steady state accretion is the sum of the parts and therefore should not be greater than 0.5 cm yr 1 under the assumptions of the model. accretion rates could deviate from this value depending on variation in plant productivity, root:shoot ratio, suspended sediment concentration, sediment capture efficiency, and episodic events.

title: invited review article: current state of research on biological effects of terahertz radiation
display_name: Invited Review Article: Current State of Research on Biological Effects of Terahertz Radiation

authorships.name: Gerald J. Wilmink
institutions: United States Air Force Research Laboratory

authorships.name: Jessica E. Grundt
institutions: United States Air Force Research Laboratory

abstract: terahertz (thz) imaging and sensing technologies are increasingly being used in a host of medical, military, and security applications. for example, thz systems are now being tested at international airports for security screening purposes, at major medical centers for cancer and burn diagnosis, and at border patrol checkpoints for identification of concealed explosives, drugs, and weapons. recent advances in thz applications have stimulated renewed interest regarding the biological effects associated with this frequency range. biological effects studies are a valuable type of basic science research because they serve to enhance our fundamental understanding of the mechanisms that govern thz interactions with biological systems. such studies are also important because they often times lay the foundation for the development of future applications. in addition, from a practical standpoint, thz biological effects research is also necessary for accurate health hazard evaluation, the development of empirically-based safety standards, and for the safe use of thz systems. given the importance and timeliness of thz bioeffects data, the purpose of this review is twofold. first, to provide readers with a common reference, which contains the necessary background concepts in biophysics and thz technology, that are required to both conduct and evaluate thz biological research. second, to provide a critical review of the scientific literature.

title: synthesis and characterization of new thiolated chitosan nanoparticles obtained by ionic gelation method
display_name: Synthesis and Characterization of New Thiolated Chitosan Nanoparticles Obtained by Ionic Gelation Method
abstract: we derivatized low molecular weight chitosan (lmwc) with 3-mercaptopropanoic acid (3-mpa) by a coupling reaction. the chemical modification of lmwc was characterized by fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ft-ir) and nuclear magnetic resonance, 1 hnmr. we researched the influence of 3-mpa on the nanoparticles formation by ionic gelation method using sodium tripolyphosphate (tpp) as cross-linker reagent. in order to optimize the nanoparticles formation, we studied the effect of the ph solution and molar ratio on nanoparticles stability. analyses of particle size, morphology, and surface charge were determined by dynamic light scattering, atomic force microscopy, and zeta potential, respectively. it was found that formation of semispherical and stable nanoparticles was improved due to the chemical modification of chitosan. optimized semispherical nanoparticles of thiolated chitosan were synthesized with the parameters (ph 4.7, molar ratios 1 : 106). additionally, we reported the thermodynamic profile of the nanoparticles formation determined by isothermal titration calorimetry (itc). the aggregation process achieved to form nanoparticles of thiolated and nonmodified chitosan consisted of two stages, considering one binding site model. gibbs free energy ( g ) and binding constant ( k a ) describe the aggregation process of thiolated chitosan/tpp, which is an initial reaction and followed by an endothermic stage. these results are promising for the possible application of these nanoparticles as nanocarriers and delivery systems.

title: environmental impacts of ecofriendly iron oxide nanoparticles on dyes removal and antibacterial activity
display_name: Environmental Impacts of Ecofriendly Iron Oxide Nanoparticles on Dyes Removal and Antibacterial Activity
abstract: abstract biosynthesized nanoparticles have a promising future since they are a more environmentally friendly, cost-effective, repeatable, and energy-efficient technique than physical or chemical synthesis. in this work, purpureocillium lilacinum was used to synthesize iron oxide nanoparticles (fe 2 o 3 -nps). characterization of mycosynthesized fe 2 o 3 -nps was done by using uv vis spectroscopy, transmission electron microscope (tem), dynamic light scattering (dls), and x-ray diffraction (xrd) analysis. uv vis gave characteristic surface plasmon resonance (spr) peak for fe 2 o 3 -nps at 380 nm. tem image reveals that the morphology of biosynthesized fe 2 o 3 -nps was hexagonal, and their size range between 13.13 and 24.93 nm. from the xrd analysis, it was confirmed the crystalline nature of fe 2 o 3 with average size 57.9 nm. further comparative study of photocatalytic decolorization of navy blue (nb) and safranin (s) using fe 2 o 3 -nps was done. fe 2 o 3 -nps exhibited potential catalytic activity with a reduction of 49.3% and 66% of navy blue and safranin, respectively. further, the antimicrobial activity of fe 2 o 3 -nps was analyzed against pathogenic bacteria ( pseudomonas aeruginosa , escherichia coli , bacillus subtilis , and staphylococcus aureus ). the fe 2 o 3 -nps were clearly more effective on gram-positive bacteria ( s. aureus and b. subtilis ) than gram-negative bacteria ( e. coli and p. aeruginosa ). thus, the mycosynthesized fe 2 o 3 -nps exhibited an ecofriendly, sustainable, and effective route for decolorization of navy blue and safranin dyes and antibacterial activity.

title: recent advances in the catalytic production of platform chemicals from holocellulosic biomass
display_name: Recent Advances in the Catalytic Production of Platform Chemicals from Holocellulosic Biomass
abstract: abstract this review discusses novel catalytic pathways of lignocellulosic biomass to value added chemicals including biomass derived sugar alcohols, organic acids, furans and biohydrocarbons. these production approaches are undertaken by biological, chemical and thermochemical transformations or a combination of them. nevertheless, the majority of research in this area is focused on the design of heterogeneous catalysts to convert value added products from holocellulosic biomass. biorefineries represent the peak of biomass processes in order to produce valuable chemicals and liquid fuels avoiding the utilization of corroding and toxic elements. the aim of the present review is to offer the readers a broad overview of recent holocellulosic based chemical and fuels production technologies via heterogeneous catalysis. there is also an overview of the economic aspects to efficiently produce these platform chemicals at industrial scale. to summarize this review, an outlook and conclusions of the reported processes to date is provided.
